shapeSummary: Black rectangular IR sensor housing (about 22 x 13.2 x 14.2 mm) with two thin mounting tabs at the rear of opposite ends, giving a 27 mm overall length. Each tab has a 2.2 mm through hole along Z. Two shallow rectangular pockets on the front face stand in for the emitter and detector windows.
warnings: Dimensions come from unverified metadata and pixel estimates.
Tab thickness, tab z-offset and tab height are guesses.
The housing's stepped profile is simplified to a single box.
The rear PCB and JST connector are omitted because their size is uncertain and they would exceed the stated Z bounds.
The window pockets are approximate in position, size and depth, and the lenses are not modeled.
Hole positions were shifted from the analysis coordinates (assumed centered in Y) to the bottom-at-Y=0 convention.

def bx(x0,x1,y0,y1,z0,z1):
    return cq.Workplane('XY').box(x1-x0,y1-y0,z1-z0,centered=False).translate((x0,y0,z0))

body = bx(-11,11,0,13.2,-7.1,7.1)
tab_l = bx(-13.5,-10,8.5,13.2,-7.1,-3.1)
tab_r = bx(10,13.5,2.0,6.9,-7.1,-3.1)
part = body.union(tab_l).union(tab_r)

# emitter and detector window pockets on the front face (+Z)
for cx in (-4.5, 3.5):
    pocket = bx(cx-3, cx+3, 3.6, 9.6, 5.1, 7.1)
    part = part.cut(pocket)

# mounting holes through the tabs (axis Z)
for (hx, hy) in ((-11.8, 11.0), (11.6, 4.4)):
    h = cq.Workplane('XY').center(hx, hy).circle(1.1).extrude(10, both=True)
    part = part.cut(h)
